svg.aria-label: How to write 静: 14 strokes · 13 pen lifts · 14 movements
svg.title: Writing 静
svg.desc: 14 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 静 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 静.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–14 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E9%9D%99.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 静, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw the left side as 情 ends: two horizontals, a vertical down through them, a long horizontal, then 月: a left side that curves to the lower left, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, and two short horizontals inside. Medians 9–14 draw the right side: a short left-falling stroke, a short horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a horizontal that turns down without lifting, a long horizontal through it, a horizontal under it, then a vertical down the middle that hooks to the left without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto runs the turned stroke on the right down past the long horizontal to the lower one.
